title: Part IV concept map
h1: Part IV Concept Map: Build It Right
description: An expandable map of Modules 08–10, connecting application architecture and tracing to evaluation, threat modeling, privacy and safety review.
lead: Part IV moves from a working prototype toward a system that can be observed, evaluated and reviewed for risk. Architecture gives the request a controlled path; evaluation measures behavior against examples and thresholds; security and responsible-AI work identify threats and add human and technical controls.
story: Route requests through explicit boundaries and manage sessions, queues and traces.
Build an evaluation set, choose metrics and use transparent release gates.
Threat-model model-enabled flows and combine privacy, safety and human review.

modules.title: AI Application Architecture
modules.tagline: Give requests controlled routes and observable state

topics.title: Gateways and model routing
topics.definition: A gateway provides a controlled interface to model services; routing selects a model or deployment for a request.
topics.example: Send an eligible low-complexity request to a lower-cost deployment and route other requests according to tested rules.
topics.finance: A bank's route must respect data classification, residency, approved deployments and fallback policy.
topics.usecase: Centralized policy, provider abstraction, observability and model selection.
topics.keep: A gateway does not make an unsafe route safe; route decisions need explicit constraints and evaluation.

topics.title: Sessions, queues and traces
topics.definition: Sessions retain task context, queues manage asynchronous work and traces correlate events across a request path.
topics.example: Attach a trace ID to retrieval and model-call events while storing only the session data needed for follow-up.
topics.finance: Support history and trace attributes should minimize sensitive content and follow access and retention rules.
topics.usecase: Multi-turn systems, background jobs, incident diagnosis and performance analysis.
topics.keep: A trace ID is not a trace system, and persistent session data needs security, retention and deletion controls.

modules.title: Evaluating GenAI Applications
modules.tagline: Test a representative dataset and gate on measurable behavior

topics.title: Build an evaluation set
topics.definition: An evaluation set contains representative inputs, expected outcomes and, where useful, human-reviewed references.
topics.example: Include routine, ambiguous and adversarial bank-support messages with expected categories and urgency.
topics.finance: Fraud and lost-card cases should be represented so important misses are visible, not averaged away.
topics.usecase: Regression tests, model comparisons and ongoing quality measurement.
topics.keep: Small or biased samples can hide failures; protect evaluation data and avoid training/evaluation leakage.
connects: compare candidate routes on the same cases

topics.title: Metrics, judges and release gates
topics.definition: Metrics summarize selected behavior; judges may score outputs, and a release gate compares results with explicit criteria.
topics.example: Track fraud recall separately from overall accuracy and block a release if the required minimum is missed.
topics.finance: A high accuracy score can still hide missed fraud messages when classes are imbalanced.
topics.usecase: Model selection, prompt regression and release decisions.
topics.keep: No single metric proves quality; automated judges need calibration and human review for important outcomes.
connects: compare route quality on the same task set

modules.title: Security and Responsible AI
modules.tagline: Threat-model the system and use layered privacy and safety controls

topics.title: Threat model and prompt injection
topics.definition: Threat modeling identifies assets, trust boundaries, threats and mitigations for an AI-enabled system.
topics.example: Treat retrieved documents and user messages as untrusted input, and prevent them from directly authorizing privileged tool calls.
topics.finance: A support assistant must not expose staff procedures or act on payment instructions embedded in retrieved content.
topics.usecase: Design reviews, abuse analysis and security testing.
topics.keep: Prompt wording and keyword indicators are not security boundaries; enforce permissions and tool rules in code.
connects: privacy and safety controls mitigate risks
route choices belong in the threat model

topics.title: Privacy, safety and human review
topics.definition: Privacy and safety controls govern what data is used, what outputs are allowed and when a person must review a result.
topics.example: Minimize customer data sent to a model and require review for a high-impact account action.
topics.finance: Masking, access control, retention, escalation and user disclosure must be designed for the actual service and jurisdiction.
topics.usecase: Reducing exposure and harm across collection, inference, storage and user interaction.
topics.keep: A regex or content filter can miss cases; use layered controls, testing and accountable review.
connects: stored data and telemetry need safeguards
